title: The eye that follows you
summary: A monster's eye in R.E.P.O. is animated rather than fixed: its pupil has a size, a multiplier and a speed of its own with a smallest and a largest, and a separate part tilts the hair on the same head on a spring.
body: The eye is a small system rather than a painted-on dot. A monster's eye target keeps its own pupil size, with a multiplier and a speed that drive it and a smallest and a largest it may reach.
It keeps the size it is at. The current pupil size is held on the target, so the eye can be somewhere between its limits instead of only at one of them.
There is a resting offset. The pupil carries an idle offset of its own, which is why an eye that is not following anything still sits somewhere rather than in the exact centre.
It can be shown for the people making the game. There is a debug flag that draws the eye target, which is a thing the build keeps for itself rather than for the shop.
The head has a second small motion. A part for the hair tilt turns and settles on a spring, with a random range and random times for when it moves, so the head is never perfectly still.
That part works on the enemy's own transform, which is how a tilt set up in one place follows the monster rather than a point in the level.
What this entry does not tell you: how far an eye tracks, how fast a pupil changes, or what the random times come to. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: An eye target keeps its own pupil size, with a multiplier, a speed and a smallest and a largest size.
It holds the current pupil size and an idle offset.
The eye target can be drawn for debugging.
A separate part tilts the head's hair on a spring, with a random range and random times.
